why: A two-storey Maelstrom warehouse on the corner of Industrial and Eisenhower Street in Northside, the place 'Scrolls before Swine' sends V to steal security footage from. Vanilla populates it only while the gig runs: the street-story quest section that carries the six-ganger spawner, their AI spots and the quest triggers streams from the unrun street story, so in the clean slate the shell stands empty. This proposal loads #sts_wat_nid_07_streetstory and activates the venue's whole community in its own initial phases, giving three Maelstrom outside and three inside at relaxed posts, with the roof hatch shut and the pre-gig door set shown. The office computer stays as the plain second-floor terminal it is; the gig's recording, the playback scene, Johnny and Aaron's confrontation stay out.

open_questions: Walk the warehouse yard at street level and check the six Maelstrom are on post. Look for two patrolling (enemy_002 and enemy_008), one standing ground (enemy_003), one leaning at the front rail (enemy_005), one on the yard dirt spot (enemy_006) and one working a tablet (enemy_007), none clustered at the spawner or frozen mid-pose.

Approach the crew and check their attitude is a normal gang-den reaction. They are Maelstrom and may go hostile when the player enters; what must not happen is a scripted gig ambush, an empty building, or bodies on the floor.

Open the street door and walk in, then leave through the garage bay and confirm both work. Both are quest-driven doors in the runtime door scope with no terminal, keycard or skill check, so they should open on plain interaction.
Check the roof hatch is shut. The env variant is set to roof_window_closed=1 / roof_window_opened=0; if the hatch still shows open (or the roof hole is visible), the variant did not apply.

Check the door meshes are the intact set. With doors_before=1 the plain closed doors should be in place; if a door hangs open or broken, or two door meshes overlap in the same frame, the doors_before/doors_after toggle is inverted.
Confirm nothing here starts the gig. There should be no map pin, no Regina holocall or brief, no journal entry and no prompt to download footage from the office computer.
Look at the office computer on the second floor and check it is a plain terminal. It is only the proximity anchor; it must not offer a personal-link disconnect or the recording.

Check the inside is walkable and not sealed by an invisible quest boundary. The sibling venue nid_02 needed its streetstory Collision_area variant set to 1; if the warehouse interior or stairs block V, that is the first thing to look for here.

communities.why: The venue's only community: six Maelstrom (faction 1 in data/factions.json) that vanilla switches on whole while the gig runs. Entry None/phase None activates every entry in its initial phase, which is exactly the crew as vanilla poses it: enemy_002 (strong shotgun) patrols, enemy_003 (the officer) stands ground, enemy_005 (grunt) leans on the front rail (phase 'a'), and enemy_006 stands on the yard dirt, enemy_007 works a tablet and enemy_008 patrols (phase 'default') - the six bodies the wiki splits into three outside and three inside. Posture is relaxed because every spot is a routine or guard_stand workspot, not an agitated shuffle or gun-ready stance; the gig's hostility comes from its graph, which never runs here.

variant_toggles.why: The intact building has its roof hatch shut. Vanilla's own pre/post-gig open-world phase (aaron_openworld) sets exactly this pair, while warehouse_combat opens the hatch for the gig's rooftop way in; closing it keeps the normal look and leaves the street doors as the way in.

The devices section holds two door sets: the intact 'before' set and the opened/broken 'after' set. Vanilla's open-world phase (and the district phase) shows doors_before; warehouse_combat shows doors_after for the fight. Showing doors_before restores the ordinary closed doors the player finds before the gig.

proximity_wait.why: The second-floor office terminal, the venue's own device and a world-streamed entity in the gameplay prefab's #loc_sts_wat_nid_07_devices section (exterior_-15_36_0_0), a few metres from the inside gangers' tablet spots. It is a computer, not a workspot, and nothing in the intact pre-gig state hides it, so the proximity wait fires as the player reaches the building. The proposal drives no action on it; it stays a plain terminal.
